piece: Suri's asset library: the Drive read, mapped and searchable by what it shows
title: Every file in Suri's Drive,
found by what it shows.
sub: How the marketing Drive became a library you can ask in words, in the order it was built.

opening.head: The library, as the team uses it

figure.query: hands only close-up in the bathroom

title: Every search started
by opening folders.
chapters.sub: The files were all there, but the folder names didn't say what was in them, and 78% didn't point to any campaign.

frame.head: How a file was found before
frame.datum: 82,615 items · 3.1 TB · 78% tied to no campaign
frame.caption: Six hands-on steps for every file

title: First it read the whole Drive,
then put every file on one map.
chapters.sub: A vision model looked at every unique image and video, whole clips included, and files that show the same thing ended up next to each other, in 60 groups.
thought: 97 h of video, every clip whole

frame.head: The Drive as mapped
frame.caption: The map, one grain for every 34 items

title: Monday's briefs and Figma's designs
went on the same map.
chapters.sub: Every Monday board it could read, and the Figma files those boards link to, now sit beside the Drive.

frame.head: Three sources, one layout

title: You ask in words or with a picture,
and land on the second in the clip.
chapters.sub: The question is read, searched three ways at once, and a model checks the top frames before anything counts as a match.
